column2: Moisten the yufka with the milk and egg mixture and roll up the filling.
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until golden on top.
Lentil mücver with zucchini and dill
1 cup cooked red lentils
Mash the lentils and mix with the zucchini, egg, flour and dill.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture onto an oiled tray.
Bake at 190°C for 25 minutes until both sides are golden.
Baked pear oat cups
2 pears
Dice the pears small and divide among baking dishes.
Mix the oats, milk, cinnamon and walnuts.
Spoon the mixture over the pears.
Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes and drizzle with honey while warm.
Zucchini and white bean soup
2 medium zucchini (diced)
1 cup cooked white beans
1 small onion (finely chopped)
4 cups hot water or vegetable stock
Heat the olive oil in a pot, fry the onion over medium heat for 4 minutes until translucent, add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the zucchini cubes and sauté for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add two-thirds of the white beans and the hot water; once boiling, cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the zucchini are very soft.
Take the pot off the heat, let it cool for 5 minutes and blend until smooth with a hand blender.
Add the remaining whole beans, season with salt and pepper and simmer for 3 more minutes; add a little hot water if too thick.
Melt the butter in a small pan, stir the mint for 10 seconds and drizzle over the soup when serving.
Leaving some of the beans whole gives the soup texture.
If using canned beans, rinse and drain well; reduce the salt.
Serve hot with a lemon wedge and toasted bread.
Carrot and celeriac soup
1 medium celeriac (about 400 g, peeled and diced)
2 carrots (sliced into rounds)
1 small onion
A pinch of nutmeg (optional)
After peeling, keep the celeriac in lemon water so it does not discolour.
Fry the chopped onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes.
Add the celeriac, carrot and potato and stir for 4 minutes.
Add the hot water; once boiling, cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes until the vegetables are easily mashed with a fork.
Take off the heat, let cool slightly and blend.
Add the milk, salt, pepper and nutmeg, heat until it just starts to simmer and serve.
The potato gives the soup a velvety texture without adding cream.
Do not boil the soup after adding the milk; it may curdle.
Serve with a few drops of olive oil and chopped parsley on top.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge; can be frozen without the milk.
Pumpkin and red lentil soup
300 g pumpkin (peeled and diced)
Half a cup red lentils (washed)
5 cups hot water
Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear.
Fry the onion and carrot in olive oil in a pot for 4 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and lentils and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the hot water; once boiling, skim off the foam and cook over low heat for 25 minutes until the lentils break down.
Blend and season with salt and cumin; add hot water if too thick.
Sizzle chilli flakes in butter and drizzle over the soup when serving; serve with lemon.
The pumpkin’s sweetness is balanced by lemon; always add a squeeze when serving.
The lentils may stick to the bottom while cooking; stir from time to time.
Serve hot with lemon and crispy bread.
Broccoli and potato soup
1 small broccoli (about 350 g, separated into florets)
1 medium potato (diced)
2 tablespoons grated kashar cheese (optional)
Separate the broccoli into florets, peel and chop the stem; set aside a few small florets in a bowl for garnish.
Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes.
Add the potato and broccoli stem, pour in the hot water and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the broccoli florets and cook for 8 more minutes until soft but still bright green.
Blend; add the milk, salt and pepper and heat without boiling.
Blanch the reserved florets for 2 minutes; serve the soup with them and the kashar cheese.
Overcooking broccoli spoils its colour and flavour; add the florets later.
Serve hot topped with kashar and blanched broccoli florets.
Cauliflower and leek soup
300 g cauliflower
1 leek (white and light green parts only, sliced into rings)
4 cups hot water or chicken stock
Half a teaspoon white pepper
1 tablespoon chopped chives or parsley
Wash the leek rings in plenty of water and remove all the grit.
Melt the butter and olive oil in a pot and soften the leek over low heat for 6 minutes without colouring.
Add the cauliflower florets and diced potato and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the hot water and bring to a boil; cook over low heat for 18 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Blend; add the milk, salt and white pepper and heat until nearly simmering.
Serve sprinkled with chives.
Not letting the leek colour while frying keeps the soup white and elegant.
Serve hot with toasted bread cubes.
Pea soup with mint
2 cups peas (fresh or frozen)
1 dessert spoon dried mint or 6 fresh mint leaves
3 tablespoons strained yogurt
Soften the chopped onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes.
Add the diced potato and hot water and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the peas; if frozen, use without thawing and cook for 6–7 minutes until soft.
Add the mint and blend; season with salt and pepper.
If too thick, add hot water and simmer for 1 more minute.
Ladle into serving bowls and put a spoonful of strained yogurt in the centre of each.
Do not overcook the peas; they should stay bright green.
Serve hot or lukewarm with yogurt and a few fresh mint leaves.
Spinach and rice soup
200 g spinach (washed and chopped)
3 tablespoons rice (washed)
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes, add the flour and fry for 1 more minute.
Whisk in the hot water, add the rice and cook over low heat for 12 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook for 5 more minutes.
Whisk the yogurt and egg yolk in a separate bowl; temper by gradually adding a few ladles of the soup.
Stir the tempered yogurt into the soup continuously and remove from the heat as soon as it starts to boil; adjust the salt.
Sprinkle with mint when serving.
If you add the yogurt without tempering it, the soup will curdle.
Serve hot with a squeeze of lemon.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge; do not boil when reheating.
Mushroom orzo soup
250 g button mushrooms (sliced)
Half a tea glass orzo
5 cups hot water or chicken stock
Heat the butter and olive oil in a pot; sauté the mushrooms over high heat for 6 minutes until they release and reabsorb their liquid.
Add the chopped onion and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the orzo and stir for 1 minute, then add the tomato paste and fry for 1 more minute.
Add the hot water; once boiling, cook over low heat for 10 minutes until the orzo is soft.
Season with salt, pepper and thyme.
Cook the mushrooms in a wide pot without crowding; otherwise they stew instead of browning.
Serve hot with lemon and chopped parsley.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge; add water when reheating, as the orzo swells over time.
Tomato soup with chickpeas
4 ripe tomatoes (grated) or 400 g canned tomatoes
A pinch of sugar (if the tomatoes are sour)
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 4 minutes, add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute, then add the grated tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Add half the chickpeas and the hot water; simmer for 12 minutes.
Blend until smooth.
Add the remaining whole chickpeas; season with salt, cumin and sugar if needed and cook for 3 more minutes.
A pinch of sugar is enough to balance the tomato’s acidity.
Serve topped with grated cheese or yogurt.
Carrot soup with ginger
5 carrots (about 500 g, sliced into rounds)
1 dessert spoon grated fresh ginger
Juice of half an orange
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes, add the ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the carrot and potato and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add the hot water; once boiling, cook over low heat for 20 minutes until the carrots are completely soft.
Take off the heat, let cool and blend.
Add the orange juice, salt and pepper and heat for 2 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and serve with yogurt in the centre.
How hot ginger tastes varies from person to person; add a little first and taste.
Serve with yogurt and toasted pumpkin seeds.
Sweet potato lentil soup
1 medium sweet potato (diced)
Half a teaspoon curry or turmeric
Wash and drain the lentils.
Fry the onion and carrot in olive oil in a pot for 4 minutes; add the curry and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the sweet potato and lentils and pour in the hot water.
Once boiling, skim off the foam and cook over low heat for 25 minutes.
Blend and adjust the salt.
Serve with a squeeze of lemon.
Sweet potato gives the soup natural sweetness; adjust the salt at the end.
Serve with toasted sesame seeds and lemon.
Chard and bulgur soup
1 bunch chard (about 300 g, finely chopped)
3 tablespoons fine bulgur
1 dessert spoon pepper paste
Finely chop the chard stems, cut the leaves into strips and wash.
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes, add the paste and stir for 1 more minute.
Add the chard stems and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add the bulgur, lentils and hot water; once boiling, cook for 15 minutes.
Add the chard leaves and cook for 5 more minutes; add the salt and mint.
Serve hot with a squeeze of lemon.
